assessment: Pixel review supports KILL as a background/correction artifact. Primary-event difference images do not repeat a stable dimming point source: sector 69 has weak positive target structure, sector 96 is dominated by a diffuse whole-cutout change, and sectors 103 and 104 show mixed positive/negative structure around the target. The sky-subtracted fixed aperture has depths of 1.012 +/- 0.395, -1.011 +/- 0.486, 6.578 +/- 0.766 and -5.333 +/- 1.132 ppt in sectors 69, 96, 103 and 104 respectively [M]. Raw aperture and sky variations closely track one another. Sector 103 has a broad step/trend, sector 96 brightens through the window, and sector 104 contains a large excursion before the window and brightening within it. These changes do not reproduce a stable transit with the fitted 2.058-ppt maximum depth. No particular nearby star is localized as an eclipsing source.
what_would_change: To reconsider: independent photometry must show repeated dimming localized to a stellar source, with a stable background and consistent depth and transit shape across sectors. Fixed-box errors use local point scatter and omit some correlated noise.
scope: Final local pixel assessment, retained after the main coordinator completed C and refreshed all six Stage D catalogues. No external submission was made.

figures.caption: Primary and phase-0.5 difference images at the accepted physical-fit ephemeris; Gaia positions are propagated to each sector epoch.

Fixed target aperture and sky variations, full phase and transit windows after sky subtraction. All four sectors use the same aperture and background geometry with a 300-arcsec Gaia cone covering the target aperture and background annulus.

background_mask_review.scope: Supplied Gaia sources on the cutout use the same fixed mask geometry. The 300-arcsec cone covers the target aperture and the background annulus, including the two-pixel source-exclusion margin; full corner coverage of a 21-by-21-pixel square is not required for that annulus.
background_mask_review.outcome: Both diagnostic figures inspected. No aperture, ephemeris, detrending or science gate was tuned.
